**Finding: Compliant (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

The LD rule is satisfied at the **preferred** level: Corio (our client, the Customer/Licensee here) pays no liquidated damages or penalties anywhere in the Agreement.

Locations inspected:
- **§ 11 Term and Termination** — termination for uncured material breach, immediate termination on insolvency, and 30-day non-renewal of the 5-year/1-year auto-renewing term. No early-termination fee, no minimum fee, no acceleration of remaining contract value. § 11.3 survives only ordinary payment obligations tied to continued Customer/Software User access and continued annual support and maintenance payments — service consideration, not a liquidated sum.
- **§ 4 Fees** and **Exhibit B Pricing / Revenue Sharing / Payment Terms** — licence, maintenance and support, MarketSite.net access, implementation (capped time-and-materials) and two-way revenue-share amounts only. Notably, there is **no late-payment interest or penalty charge** at all.
- **§ 4.4 Audit Rights** — Corio reimburses reasonable examination cost only if an audit reveals underpayment over 5%. Noted in the rationale as a cost-reimbursement mechanic, not a liquidated or penal amount, so not flagged.
- **§ 9 Limitation of Liability** — a mutual cap and consequential-damages waiver; a liability ceiling, not a Customer-payable liquidated amount.
- Targeted searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "damages", "minimum", "interest/late/overdue", "non-refundable/forfeit/remaining term", and "shall pay … an amount equal to" returned no Customer-payable liquidated mechanic.

Because the clause set meets the preferred position, no fallback cap (3 months' fees) needs to be negotiated and no redline was proposed, consistent with the instruction not to redline a clause that already meets the playbook target.
